newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 29.

text.p: MP Morgan's European trip paid by Maori TV: NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan went to Europe at the expense of taxpayer-funded Aotearoa Television Network four days after being elected to Parliament in October last year. Page 1.
Cabinet gives green light to $94 million building: The Cabinet decided on Monday to go ahead with a $94 million ministerial building, insisting the project was not lavish indulgence. Page 1.

MP harassed me -- Fletcher: Women's Affairs Minister Christine Fletcher says she was sexually harassed at Parliament by a male MP who, during her first term as an MP, asked her every day who was looking after her children. Page 1.

Moore's call on fisheries denounced by Maori leaders: Labour MP Mike Moore's call for the government to intervene in the Maori fisheries debate was denounced by Maori MPs and leaders on Monday as an example of the patronising attitude that led Maoris to abandon the Labour Party in droves. Page 2.
SFO boss gets extra days for sick leave: Serious Fraud Office boss Chas Sturt's sick leave had been extended, acting director David Bradshaw said on Monday. Page 2.

Bolger steps into cardiac services row: Prime Minister Jim Bolger has been drawn into a dispute between Health Minister Bill English and his NZ First associate, Neil Kirton, on whether a private-public tender for Christchurch cardiac services should go ahead. Page 2.

Beer sales slump takes toll on Lion: A continuing slump in beer sales on both sides of the Tasman has taken a toll on Lion Nathan's fortunes, with its interim tax-paid of $72.2 million down 20.8 percent for the six months to February. Page 11.

DB staying on target, says chief: Brewer DB Group remained on track to match last year's first-half profit, despite an overall shrinking beer market in New Zealand, DB Breweries chief executive Brian Blake said on Monday. Page 11.
Fletcher Energy production up: Fletcher Energy incresed oil and gas production 37 percent in the March quarter to 12.86 million barrels of oil equivalent, the company said on Monday. Page 11.

Timberwest reports third-quarter boost: Timberwest Forest, a 51 percent-held offshoot of Fletcher Challenge Canada, reported a jump in after-tax net earnings to C$7.6 million (NZ$7.9 million) for the third quarter to March, compared with C$700,000 for the corresponding period of 1996. Page 11.
ASB lifts profit 37pc: ASB Bank on Monday reported a 37 percent jump in after tax operating profit for the March quarter. Page 11.
'Telenotes' issued: Telecom on Monday announced the issue of $275 million in "Telenotes" by finance subsidiary TCNZ Finance. Page 11.
Survey shows unique absense: New Zealand is the bottom of the heap when it comes to environmental reporting, according to a survey of 13 countries by business advisers KPMG issued on Monday. Page 11.

Resource Act being abused says Bradford: The Resource Management Act is increasingly being used against new projects to stop competition, for financial gain or for political purposes, according to Energy and Business Development Minister Max Bradford. Page 12.

Richina decides to suspend dividend plan: Richina Pacific has said it will suspend its dividend reinvestment plan for a dividend payment on May 15 to protect shareholders with a standing nomination to receive shares in lieu of a dividend. Page 12.

ECNZ questions need to fragment: State generator ECNZ questioned the sense in further fragmentation of power generation, saying this could cause a conflict that was not in the taxpayers' interest. Page 12.
